bullets.text: Underwriting profit margin fell 6.7 pts to 1.7% from 8.4% in 1998; EPS fell to $3.96 from $6.11; Personal Lines underwriting profit margin dropped to 1.2% from 7.9%.
Rates cut 1.3% in early 1999 but raised 4.4% in second half; abandoned policyholder lifetime profit targets, returning to a calendar-year 96 combined ratio goal and calendar-year manager incentives.

Sudden reversal in accident frequency and severity trends raised loss costs; claims handled reached 988,000; prior-year reserve reductions shrank to 0.5 combined ratio points versus 3.7 points in 1998.
Annual premium volume +16% to $6,124.7M (20% CAGR since 1994); Personal Lines NPW +16% to $5,702.4M (93% of total); became the 4th largest U.S. auto insurer.

Debt-to-capital 27.6%; issued $300M 30-year 6.625% notes to refinance 2000 maturities; pre-tax investment income $387.9M; equities returned 11.6% versus Russell 3000's 20.9% due to underweighting technology; no discretionary share buybacks.

Pursues a multi-distribution approach viewing no channel as superior; provides independent agents with desktop software and 24/7 contact for questions, focusing on competitive pricing, ease of doing business, and point-of-sale customer experience.
Extended online auto dominance, selling >$70M over the Internet (~7% of direct sales); offered online purchasing across 47 states and DC, generating >1M quotes and servicing >65,000 customers.

Super Bowl XXXIII advertising incurred significant costs without proportionate benefits; awareness grew among age segments up to 35; changed ad agencies, and 2000 advertising features Progressive employees explaining company advantages.

Auto cycle appeared to turn in 1999; ongoing consolidation will probably yield fewer, stronger competitors; multiple-line insurers exiting personal lines could benefit Progressive as the leading auto insurer through independent agents.

Launching homeowners insurance in Arizona in March 2000, including condominium and renters policies, with selective multi-state rollout restricted to states with adequate rate levels and reasonable underwriting profit opportunity.
